items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Coltrane notwithstanding. I’m sure he made a valuable contribution... Coltrane had his thing, which just didn’t appeal to me that much.

ctx.x: You say it’s interesting, but the statement you made to the student, would you stand by that and say that Charlie Parker was the last innovation that you found to be a true departure or a true . . .
For me, yes. For me, yes, Coltrane notwithstanding. I’m sure he made a valuable contribution, but, you know, I think Parker did it. I’m still amazed by it.

While we’re on the subject of Charlie Parker, you did work with him on occasion in recording situations, and I believe you said you did have an opportunity to talk to him and have a conversation with him.
